title: They thought they were ready—until Jesus told them to leave everything behind.
paragraphs: They thought they were ready—until Jesus told them to leave everything behind.

No backup plan.
No extra money.
No second pair of clothes.
Just obedience.
You would have hesitated too.
Because everything in you has been trained to prepare, to secure, to control outcomes. You don’t move unless you know how it will end. You don’t step unless provision is visible.
But then comes that command that feels almost reckless:
“Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses.” (Matthew 10:9)
Read that again.
He wasn’t just sending them out. He was stripping them of their illusions.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior

The scene feels quiet at first. Dust under their feet. The weight of the unknown pressing into their chest. These weren’t superhumans. These were ordinary men who had seen miracles—but now they were being asked to live one.

No money meant no control.
No extra supplies meant no safety net.
And that’s exactly the point.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Jesus wasn’t teaching them survival.
He was teaching them dependence.

You say you trust God—but your life is padded with contingencies.
Savings you rely on more than prayer.
Plans that replace obedience.
Comfort that silences calling.
God saw it.
You knew.

You’ve delayed obedience because you didn’t feel “ready.”
You’ve said, “I just need a little more security first.”
But deep down, you weren’t waiting on God—you were waiting on certainty.
And certainty is the one thing faith will never give you.
This is where it breaks.
Because following Jesus will eventually lead you to a moment where preparation is no longer enough. Where logic runs out. Where control slips through your fingers.
And you’re left with one question:
Do you actually trust Him?
Silence answers louder than words.
The disciples had to walk into towns not knowing who would receive them. They had to depend on strangers for food. They had to preach a message that could get them rejected—or worse.
And still, they went.
Why?
Because something in them had already shifted. They had seen enough of Jesus to know this:
If He sends you, He sustains you.
But that truth doesn’t comfort you if you’re still trying to hold onto control.
This is where Scripture cuts deeper:
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.” (Proverbs 3:5)

Not some.
All.

That includes your future.
Your provision.
Your reputation.
Everything.

You don’t partially follow Jesus.
You either trust Him… or you replace Him.
And that’s the hidden sin here.
Not just fear—but self-reliance disguised as wisdom.

You’ve called it “being responsible.”
But sometimes it’s just unbelief wearing a respectable face.
God saw it.
You knew.
Now the tension tightens.
Because the same Jesus who told them to go without supplies also said this:
“Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you.” (Matthew 6:33)
That’s the promise.
But the condition is where most people walk away.
Seek first.

Not after you’re stable.
Not after you’re comfortable.
Not after you’ve secured your life.
First.
This is where everything flips.

Because the lesson wasn’t about poverty—it was about priority.
Not about lack—but about lordship.
Who actually provides for you?

Your job?
Your plans?
Your intelligence?
Or God?
Your answer shows up in how tightly you hold everything.
And then comes the Gospel.
Because here’s the deeper truth—you weren’t just sent unprepared.
You were born separated.
Sin left you spiritually bankrupt. No righteousness. No backup plan. No way to save yourself.
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)

Jesus didn’t wait for you to get ready.
He stepped into your lack.
On the cross, He took everything you couldn’t carry—your sin, your guilt, your failure—and paid for it in full.
“It is finished.” (John 19:30)

That means your striving ends here.
Your attempts to secure yourself end here.
Grace begins where your control dies.
And now you stand in the same place the disciples once stood.
Sent.

Not with everything figured out.
But with everything you need in Him.
So what will you do?
Will you keep delaying obedience until it feels safe?
Or will you step into the uncomfortable, unplanned, God-dependent life you were actually called to live?
Because one path keeps you in control—and far from transformation.
The other strips you… but leads you straight into the power and provision of God.
There’s something in you right now that knows this is true.
Don’t ignore it.
Say it plainly—“I’ve been trusting myself more than God.” Let that come out of your mouth. Let it be real.
Someone you know is stuck in that same place—send this to them. Not casually. Intentionally.
You’re going to feel this tension again. And when you do, you’ll need to remember what God is asking of you.
If you’re ready to go deeper—to be corrected, stretched, and grounded in truth beyond surface-level faith—you can step into that here:
This isn’t about information.
It’s about transformation.
